descripcion_es: Choosing words to suit the situation.
resumen: Many ideas can be expressed with formal words (of Latin origin), neutral words or informal ones (often phrasal verbs). Choosing the right register is essential in a presentation, an email or a report.

explicacion.texto: Rule of thumb: in English, the word of Latin origin is usually the formal one (obtain, require, commence), and the phrasal verb or the short word is the neutral or informal one (get, need, start). Spanish speakers find the Latin word natural, so they tend to sound too formal in conversation.

filas: to get or achieve something (es: obtener, conseguir)
to bring to an end (es: terminar)
to have your home somewhere (es: residir, vivir)
to move to a later time (es: aplazar)
to examine the facts (es: investigar, examinar)
to get to know a fact (es: averiguar)
to make smaller or less (es: reducir)
to decide that something will not happen (es: suspender, cancelar)
introduces a contrast (es: sin embargo / pero)
introduces a result (es: por tanto / así que)
a large amount of (es: un montón de)
intention or wish, spoken only (es: voy a / quiero, solo oral)

items: Formal texts avoid contractions (don't → do not) and very informal phrasal verbs.
In conversation, too much formality sounds stiff: “I will assist you” versus “I'll help you”.
Formal email: “I am writing to enquire about…”, “I look forward to hearing from you”; informal: “Just a quick note to ask…”, “Speak soon”.

ejemplos.frase: Passengers are required to show a valid ticket.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se exige a los pasajeros que muestren un billete válido.

ejemplos.frase: We had to put off the meeting until next week.
ejemplos.traduccion: Tuvimos que aplazar la reunión hasta la semana que viene.

ejemplos.frase: I am writing to enquire about the vacancy advertised on your website.
ejemplos.traduccion: Le escribo para informarme sobre la vacante anunciada en su web.

ejemplos.frase: The police are looking into the incident.
ejemplos.traduccion: La policía está investigando el incidente.

ejemplos.frase: I can't put up with this heat any more.
Applications must be submitted prior to 30 June.
ejemplos.traduccion: Las solicitudes deben presentarse antes del 30 de junio.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Hi Tom! I would like to inform you that I'm coming on Friday.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Hi Tom! Just to let you know I'm coming on Friday.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: With a friend, “inform” is too formal.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Dear Sir, I wanna know the price.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Dear Sir, I would like to know the price.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: We must reduce down the costs.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: We must cut down on costs.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Don't mix the Latin verb with the particle: either “reduce costs” or “cut down on costs”.

ejercicios.frase: Visitors ___ a permit to enter the archive.
respuestas: require
ejercicios.explicacion: The table in this unit pairs require (formal) with need (neutral): both mean “to need something” (es: necesitar, requerir). The instruction asks for the most formal option, and the context (a notice about an archive, visitors, permit) is typical of formal written register. That is why the answer is require. Need would be correct in a conversation, but it is not the most formal.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los visitantes necesitan un permiso para entrar en el archivo.

por_opcion.require: Correct: it is the formal equivalent of need, typical of notices and rules.
por_opcion.need: It is grammatically correct and means the same, but it is neutral, not the most formal.
por_opcion.have got to have: An informal and redundant expression (“they have to have”); unsuitable for a notice.
por_opcion.wanna have: Wanna is a spoken contraction of want to; as well as being informal, it changes the meaning.

glosario.definicion_l: require as useful, just, or proper · consider obligatory; request and expect
a legal document giving official permission to do something · the act of giving a formal (usually written) authorization

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the informal phrasal verb equivalent to “postpone” (in the past).
ejercicios.frase: They ___ off the wedding because of the storm.
respuestas: put
ejercicios.explicacion: The unit gives put off as the neutral or informal equivalent of postpone (es: aplazar). The gap comes before off, so only the verb put is missing, and its past form is the same: put. The unit warns not to confuse it with call off, which means “cancel”: the wedding is delayed, not cancelled.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Put off” = postpone (es: aplazar); “call off” means cancel, not postpone.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aplazaron la boda por la tormenta.

errores_previstos.respuesta: called
errores_previstos.explicacion: Call off means cancel; the instruction asks for the equivalent of postpone: put off.

errores_previstos.respuesta: putted
errores_previstos.explicacion: Put is irregular and its past form is the same: put.

errores_previstos.respuesta: postponed
errores_previstos.explicacion: That is the formal verb; the instruction asks for the phrasal verb, and off is already in the sentence: put.

glosario.definicion_l: hold back to a later time · cause to feel intense dislike or distaste
a violent weather condition with winds 64-72 knots (11 on the Beaufort scale) and precipitation and thunder and lightning · a violent commotion or disturbance

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the right option for a formal email.
ejercicios.frase: I am writing to ___ about the job you advertised.
respuestas: enquire
ejercicios.explicacion: The unit gives I am writing to enquire about… as an opening formula for a formal email. Enquire (or inquire, more American) is the formal equivalent of ask and means “to ask for information”. The clue is I am writing, with no contraction, typical of a formal letter. Advertise means to announce publicly, in this case a job vacancy.
ejercicios.traduccion: Le escribo para informarme sobre el puesto que han anunciado.

por_opcion.enquire: Correct: the formal verb for “to ask for information”, and enquire about is the standard formula.
por_opcion.ask you stuff: Very informal (stuff = things); unsuitable for a formal email.
por_opcion.check out: An informal phrasal verb meaning “to have a look at” or “to check”; it does not fit with about or with the register.
por_opcion.find: Find means to discover something; find about is ungrammatical (it would be find out about, and that is informal too).

glosario.definicion_l: call attention to · make publicity for; try to sell (a product)

ejercicios.enunciado: Make it more formal by replacing the verb “get” with a formal one.
ejercicios.frase: You can get more information at reception.
respuestas: You can obtain more information at reception.
Further information can be obtained at reception.
More information can be obtained at reception.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table in this unit gives obtain as the formal equivalent of get (es: obtener, conseguir). You just replace the verb: You can obtain more information at reception. Passive versions are also accepted, Further information can be obtained, very typical of formal notices; further is the formal form of more in this context.
ejercicios.traduccion: Puede obtener más información en recepción.

errores_previstos.respuesta: You can take more information at reception.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Take is not the formal equivalent of get in this sense; the answer is obtain.

errores_previstos.respuesta: You can obtein more information at reception.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Spelling mistake: obtain is spelt with ai.

errores_previstos.respuesta: You can get more information at reception.
errores_previstos.explicacion: That is the original sentence: you need to replace get with obtain.

glosario.definicion_l: come into possession of · receive a specified treatment (abstract)
the manner in which something is greeted · a formal party of people; as after a wedding

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the most natural option in a conversation with friends.
ejercicios.frase: Can you ___ me move this sofa?
respuestas: help
ejercicios.explicacion: The unit warns that, in conversation, too much formality sounds stiff, and it pairs assist (formal) with help (neutral). The clue is the context: a conversation between friends about moving a sofa. The natural choice is help. Also, help allows the structure help me move, without to, whereas assist me move would be ungrammatical.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Among friends we use “help”; “assist” and “aid” are formal.

por_opcion.help: Correct: a neutral, natural verb among friends; it allows help me move.
por_opcion.assist: It is formal (customer service, official texts) and does not allow assist me move: it would be assist me in moving or assist me to move.
por_opcion.aid: It is formal or technical (first aid, humanitarian aid); it sounds very strange in a conversation.

glosario.definicion_l: the activity of contributing to the fulfillment of a need or furtherance of an effort or purpose · a person who contributes to the fulfillment of a need or furtherance of an effort or purpose
the activity of contributing to the fulfillment of a need or furtherance of an effort or purpose · (sports) the act of enabling another player to make a good play
a person or thing that is a resource that helps make something easier or possible to do · the activity of contributing to the fulfillment of a need or furtherance of an effort or purpose

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the neutral phrasal verb equivalent to “investigate”.
ejercicios.frase: The manager promised to look ___ the complaint.
respuestas: into
ejercicios.explicacion: The table in this unit gives look into as the neutral equivalent of investigate (es: investigar, examinar). The particle look needs for this meaning is into. Complaint means an expression of dissatisfaction (es: queja, reclamación). Look at would mean “to direct your eyes at” and look for “to search for”, which change the meaning.
ejercicios.traduccion: El gerente prometió estudiar la reclamación.

errores_previstos.respuesta: at
errores_previstos.explicacion: Look at means to direct your eyes at something; the equivalent of investigate is look into.

errores_previstos.respuesta: for
errores_previstos.explicacion: Look for means to search for; for “investigate, study” it is look into.

errores_previstos.respuesta: in
errores_previstos.explicacion: The correct particle of the phrasal verb is into: look into.

glosario.definicion_l: investigate scientifically · examine so as to determine accuracy, quality, or condition
an often persistent bodily disorder or disease; a cause for complaining · (formerly) a loud cry (or repeated cries) of pain or rage or sorrow
someone who controls resources and expenditures · (sports) someone in charge of training an athlete or a team

ejercicios.frase: Dear Ms Smith, I wanna apply for the post of accountant.
respuestas: Dear Ms Smith, I would like to apply for the post of accountant.
Dear Ms Smith, I wish to apply for the post of accountant.
Dear Ms Smith, I am writing to apply for the post of accountant.
ejercicios.explicacion: The unit explains that gonna and wanna are informal, spoken-only forms that are avoided in formal texts. The clue is the greeting Dear Ms Smith, typical of a formal email. You need to replace wanna with I would like to, I wish to or the formula I am writing to. Apply for means to formally request a job, and an accountant is a person who keeps financial accounts (es: contable).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Wanna” is informal and spoken; in a formal email: “I would like to”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estimada Sra. Smith: quisiera solicitar el puesto de contable.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Dear Ms Smith, I wanna apply for the post of accountant.
errores_previstos.explicacion: That is the uncorrected sentence: wanna is informal and spoken.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Dear Ms Smith, I want apply for the post of accountant.
errores_previstos.explicacion: To is missing (want to apply), and even then want sounds too direct: I would like to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Dear Ms Smith, I'm gonna apply for the post of accountant.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Gonna is as informal as wanna and it also changes the meaning (es: voy a); in a formal email: I would like to.

glosario.definicion_l: United States aviator who in 1933 made the first solo flight around the world (1899-1935) · United States female author who wrote a book and a syndicated newspaper column on etiquette (1872-1960)
someone who maintains and audits business accounts

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the formal option equivalent to “enough”.
ejercicios.frase: There is not ___ evidence to support the claim.
respuestas: sufficient
ejercicios.explicacion: The table in this unit pairs sufficient (formal) with enough (neutral), both meaning “as much as needed” (es: suficiente). The context, with evidence and claim (a statement that something is true), is typical of a report or an academic text. Sufficient goes before the noun, like enough. Evidence is uncountable: it takes no -s.
ejercicios.traduccion: No hay pruebas suficientes que respalden la afirmación.

por_opcion.sufficient: Correct: the formal equivalent of enough, typical of reports and academic texts.
por_opcion.plenty: Plenty means “more than enough, a lot” and needs of (plenty of); it also changes the meaning.
por_opcion.loads of: Very informal (es: un montón de) and it changes the meaning: it does not mean “as much as needed”.
por_opcion.a lot: It means “much, many” and would need of; it is not equivalent to enough, and it is neutral, not formal.

glosario.definicion_l: of a quantity that can fulfill a need or requirement but without being abundant
your basis for belief or disbelief; knowledge on which to base belief · an indication that makes something evident
an assertion of a right (as to money or property) · an assertion that something is true or factual

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the informal phrasal verb equivalent to “tolerate”.
ejercicios.frase: I don't know how you put up ___ his jokes.
respuestas: with
ejercicios.explicacion: The unit gives put up with as the informal equivalent of tolerate (es: aguantar, soportar). It is a three-word phrasal verb, and the last word is the preposition with, which introduces what you tolerate. Without with, put up means something else (to give someone a bed for the night, to hang something on a wall).
ejercicios.traduccion: No sé cómo aguantas sus bromas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: to
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition of this phrasal verb is with: put up with.

errores_previstos.respuesta: off
errores_previstos.explicacion: Put off means postpone; for “tolerate” it is put up with.

errores_previstos.respuesta: on
errores_previstos.explicacion: Put up on does not exist with this meaning: put up with.

glosario.definicion_l: a humorous anecdote or remark intended to provoke laughter · activity characterized by good humor

ejercicios.frase: Please read the instructions ___ using the device.
respuestas: prior to
ejercicios.explicacion: The table in this unit pairs prior to (formal) with before (neutral), “earlier than” (es: antes de). The context, instructions for an appliance, is formal and written. Prior to is a preposition, so it is followed by -ing (prior to using), just like before using. Device means a machine or piece of equipment (es: aparato, dispositivo).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Prior to” is the formal form of “before”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Lea las instrucciones antes de utilizar el aparato.

por_opcion.prior to: Correct: a formal preposition equivalent to before.
por_opcion.before of: A calque of Spanish “antes de”: before does not take of.
por_opcion.previous: Previous is an adjective (“earlier”); it cannot introduce using.
por_opcion.ahead: Ahead is an adverb (“in front, forward”); ahead of would be possible but not ahead alone, and it is not the formal form of before.

glosario.definicion_l: an instrumentality invented for a particular purpose · something in an artistic work designed to achieve a particular effect

ejercicios.enunciado: Make it neutral: replace “purchase” with an everyday verb.
ejercicios.frase: I purchased a new laptop yesterday.
respuestas: I bought a new laptop yesterday.
I got a new laptop yesterday.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table in this unit gives purchase as the formal form of buy (es: comprar). In everyday conversation the natural choice is buy, in the past bought. The unit also accepts got, which in informal language can mean “obtained, bought for yourself”. Purchase works well in invoices or business texts, but not when telling someone what you did yesterday.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ayer me compré un portátil nuevo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I buyed a new laptop yesterday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Buy is irregular: the past form is bought.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I buy a new laptop yesterday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With yesterday you need the past: bought.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I acquired a new laptop yesterday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Acquire is formal too; the instruction asks for an everyday verb, bought.

glosario.definicion_l: the acquisition of something for payment · something acquired by purchase
a portable computer small enough to use in your lap

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the informal word equivalent to “children”.
ejercicios.frase: We took the ___ to the beach on Sunday.
respuestas: kids
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table in this unit pairs kids (informal) with children (neutral). The context, a family plan for Sunday, is informal, so kids is the natural choice. Offspring means a person's or animal's descendants (es: descendencia) and is formal or biological; minors are people under the legal age of adulthood (es: menores de edad).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Kids” is the informal form; “offspring” and “minors” are formal or technical.
ejercicios.traduccion: El domingo llevamos a los niños a la playa.

por_opcion.kids: Correct: an informal and very common form of children.
por_opcion.offspring: It means “descendants” (es: descendencia, prole); it is formal or technical and sounds strange in a conversation.
por_opcion.minors: It means people under the legal age (es: menores de edad); it is only used in legal or administrative contexts.

glosario.definicion_l: English dramatist (1558-1594) · a young person of either sex
the immediate descendants of a person · something that comes into existence as a result
a league of teams that do not belong to a major league (especially baseball)

ejercicios.frase: I look forward to ___ from you.
respuestas: hearing
ejercicios.explicacion: The unit gives I look forward to hearing from you as a formal email closing. Here to is a preposition, not the infinitive marker, so it is followed by -ing: hearing. Hear from someone means to receive news from someone. The typical mistake is writing to hear, by analogy with other verbs.
ejercicios.traduccion: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.

errores_previstos.respuesta: hear
errores_previstos.explicacion: In look forward to, to is a preposition and is followed by -ing: hearing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: listening
errores_previstos.explicacion: Listen means to pay attention to sounds; “to receive news from” is hear from: hearing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: heard
errores_previstos.explicacion: After the preposition to comes the gerund: hearing.

glosario.significado: esperar con interés, tener ganas de

ejercicios.enunciado: Put the words in order (formal register).
respuestas: Passengers are required to show their tickets
ejercicios.explicacion: The unit explains that be required to is a formal passive meaning “to be obliged to”. The order is subject (Passengers) + are required + to + infinitive (show) + object (their tickets). It is a typical structure in official notices, more formal than Passengers must show or have to show.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Formal passive “be required to” = to be obliged to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se exige a los pasajeros que muestren sus billetes.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Passengers are required their tickets to show
errores_previstos.explicacion: After required comes the to-infinitive and then the object: to show their tickets.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Passengers are to show required their tickets
errores_previstos.explicacion: The passive is formed with are required, followed by to show.

glosario.definicion_l: a traveler riding in a vehicle (a boat or bus or car or plane or train etc.) who is not operating it

ejercicios.frase: The company must reduce down its costs.
respuestas: The company must reduce its costs.
The company must cut down on its costs.
The company must cut its costs.
ejercicios.explicacion: The unit pairs reduce (formal) with cut down (on) (neutral). The mistake is mixing the two: reduce is a single-word verb and takes no particle, so reduce down is wrong. There are three solutions: reduce its costs (formal), cut its costs or cut down on its costs (more informal), and all three are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Reduce” takes no particle; the phrasal verb is “cut down on”.
ejercicios.traduccion: La empresa debe reducir sus costes.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The company must reduce down its costs.
errores_previstos.explicacion: That is the uncorrected sentence: reduce takes no particle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The company must cut on its costs.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The particle down is missing: the phrasal verb is cut down on (or simply cut its costs).

errores_previstos.respuesta: The company must reduce down on its costs.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It still mixes registers: either reduce without a particle or cut down on.

glosario.definicion_l: cut down on; make a reduction in · make less complex

descripcion_larga_es: In English the same idea can be expressed with a formal word of Latin origin (obtain, require, commence), a neutral one (get, need, start) or an informal one, often a phrasal verb (put up with, call off). Choosing the right register is key in a presentation, an email or a report. Spanish speakers tend to pick the Latin word, which feels familiar, and sound too formal in conversation.

contexto.que_es: Register is the degree of formality of language: formal, neutral or informal. In English it shows above all in vocabulary (Latin words versus short words or phrasal verbs), in the use of contractions and in the set formulas of letters and emails.
contexto.por_que_importa: The wrong register does not stop people understanding you, but it gives the wrong impression: “wanna” in a letter of application looks careless, and “I shall assist you” among friends sounds stiff or ironic. In a writing exam or a professional oral presentation, appropriate register is an explicit assessment criterion. For an economist, mastering formal written English and neutral spoken English is essential.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: Formal register is used in reports, official emails, notices, regulations and presentations; neutral register in most work conversations; informal register with friends and in informal messages. The clues are the recipient (Dear Ms Smith versus Hi Tom), the type of text and the topic. Spanish speakers tend to use Latinate words in conversation and, at the same time, slip informal expressions into formal texts.
